trial_court: Family Court, Shimla District Shimla (Principal Judge, Family Court, vide judgment dated 30.11.2023)
case_name: Vijay Sharma vs Sheetal Sharma And Anr

parties.respondent_defendant: Sheetal Sharma and Anr. (wife and another)

facts_of_case: Petitioner filed a petition seeking custody of minor Lavish Sharma. Marriage between parties was solemnized as per Hindu Rites and Customs at Sisra on 14.09.2015. Differences arose, respondent No.1 left her matrimonial home in August 2021 with the minor.

legal_principles.principle: Courts must be cautious and act with great circumspection in dealing with claims for letting in additional evidence, particularly at the appellate stage after a long lapse of time.
legal_principles.held: The courts shall have to be cautious and must always act with great circumspection in dealing with the claims for letting in additional evidence particularly, in the form of oral evidence at the appellate stage and that too, after a long lapse of time.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 — Order 41 Rule 27

legal_principles.principle: A belated application for additional evidence at the appellate stage may not be entertained.
legal_principles.held: The attempt, the High Court ascribed it to be a stage-managed affair in order to somehow defeat the claim of the respondents -- and having had the privilege of perusal of record we lend our concurrence thereto and the finding of the High Court cannot be found fault with for rejecting the prayer of the appellants for additional evidence made in the belated application.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 — Order 41 Rule 27

legal_principles.principle: A document sought to be produced at the appellate stage must satisfy the requirement of Order 41 Rule 27 of CPC.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, these documents do not satisfy the requirement of Order 41 Rule 27 of CPC and cannot be taken on record.
applicable_acts_sections: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 — Order 41 Rule 27

legal_principles.principle: An objection to the place of suing must be taken at the first instance and a decree passed by the Court of first instance.
legal_principles.held: It was laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Om Prakash Agarwal v. Vishan Dayal Rajpoot, (2019) 14 SCC 526: (2020) 1 SCC (Civ) 731: 2018 SCC OnLine SC 1942 that the objection to the jurisdiction has to be taken at the first instance and a decree passed by the Court of first instance.
cited_cases: Om Prakash Agarwal v. Vishan Dayal Rajpoot, (2019) 14 SCC 526: (2020) 1 SCC (Civ) 731: 2018 SCC OnLine SC 1942

outcome.final_order: Petition seeking custody of minor was ordered to be dismissed by the trial court.
